events.objective: Establish the true symptom signature and onset: determine exactly when customer-reported transfer failures began (~12:15-12:32Z) and characterize them. Critically, verify whether the 'green' payment-service error_rate panel is trustworthy by decomposing the failure: check logs/metrics for transfer-specific signals (business declines, async callbacks, timeouts, downstream gRPC/HTTP calls from payment-service to its dependencies, queue depth, retry counts, latency percentiles) and for outbound connection errors/timeouts to the bank/acquirer. Report which services/methods/paths are actually failing and at what rate, and whether failures are visible in any signal at all. Also check resource trends (CPU/mem/thread pool/connection pool) on payment-service and immediate downstreams over 11:00-14:00Z.

Find what changed across ALL services in the payment path in the window 2026-04-02T10:00Z to 13:59Z: list deploys, config changes, feature-flag/credential changes (particularly anything touching bank/acquirer integration, transfer limits, retries, timeouts, auth) — not just in payment-service but in any service payment-service depends on. Map the dependency graph around payment-service and the fund-transfer path (including shared components, queues, ledgers, external bank connectors) and identify shared components that other healthy services also use. Also search historical incidents for precedents: prior 'dashboard green but customers failing', bank/acquirer outages, or blind-spot failure modes, and report what the root cause was.

args.query: dashboard green but customers failing payment failures
bank acquirer connector outage timeout retry transfer
silent failure missing metrics blind spot monitoring gap

events.statement: Across ALL services in 10:00-13:59Z only one deploy occurred: settlement-service v1.9.0 at 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z ('new CSV exporter'), status live, not rolled back. payment-service itself had no deploy in the window.

Exactly one config change in the window: payment-service 'bank.api.timeout_ms' raised 3000 -> 5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair ('Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory') — i.e. the bank/acquirer call timeout was changed roughly 72 min before the incident was reported (12:32Z).

Fund-transfer path edges: api-gateway -> payment-service (http); payment-service -> ledger-db (db), -> bank-partner-api (external), -> kafka (queue-produce). bank-partner-api has has_telemetry=false, so there is no telemetry for the bank leg of the transfer path.

ledger-db and kafka are flagged shared=true. ledger-db has four writer services (order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service, settlement-service), and settlement-service consumes kafka while also writing ledger-db — so settlement-service sits on both shared components payment-service uses.

Precedent HIST-105 (2025-11-19, payment-service): 'Payment failures: bank partner API outage', root cause 'Bank partner API returned 5xx for 40 minutes (their incident)', category dependency_failure, resolution 'Waited for partner; queued retries' — the closest prior match to today's symptom of customer-visible payment failures from the bank/acquirer leg. HIST-103 (order/exchange-gateway, 2025-10-21) is the same external-partner-outage pattern.

Other precedents touching payment-path components with silent/blind-spot failure modes: HIST-106 settlement-service expired mTLS client cert (tls handshake failures), HIST-114 ledger-db disk full from retained WAL (write failures), HIST-109 auth-service JWT clock-skew regression after library upgrade. These are leads only, not evidence about the current incident.

Inference: with no payment-service deploy, the only observed changes in the window are the 11:20Z bank.api.timeout_ms raise (3000->5000) and the 10:30Z settlement-service v1.9.0 deploy, whose new exporter writes the shared ledger-db that payment-service also writes. Both are candidates for a green-dashboard-but-customer-visible payment failure, but I did not confirm either as the cause.

events.description: No metrics, traces or service logs were queried (budget exhausted after dependency/config/deploy/history calls); I cannot show payment-service or ledger-db metric values across 10:00-13:59Z to confirm whether any resource-level signal moved.
bank-partner-api is external with has_telemetry=false, and no credential/feature-flag change for the bank connector appears in the config-change results.

Config/deploy queries returned only a single item each across 'all services'; no explicit credential-rotation or feature-flag tool was available, so flag/credential state for the payment path is unchecked.
Historical search returned only 5+2+1 incidents; no incident was found whose title explicitly matches 'dashboard green but customers failing' as a monitoring gap.

events.answer: In 10:00-13:59Z the payment path saw exactly two changes: settlement-service v1.9.0 deployed 10:30Z (CSV exporter, live) and payment-service config bank.api.timeout_ms raised 3000->5000 at 11:20Z after a 'partner advisory'; payment-service itself had no deploy. The transfer path is api-gateway -> payment-service -> {ledger-db (shared, 4 writers), bank-partner-api (external, no telemetry), kafka (shared)}; settlement-service touches both shared components. Prior art: HIST-105 (2025-11-19) was a bank partner API 5xx outage with the same customer-visible symptom, HIST-106/114/109 show credential-expiry and shared-datastore failure modes on these same components — leads only, no root cause confirmed here.

events.statement: payment-service error_rate (HTTP 5xx) stayed flat/normal throughout 11:00-14:00Z, avg ~0.22% (min 0.1, max 0.32), showing NO incident — this is why the dashboard looked green. The panel only measures 'HTTP 5xx' and the failures are async PENDING_RETRY, so they never register as 5xx.

The transfer-specific signal bank_api_error_rate jumped from a stable ~0.2% to 100%: 0.20% at 12:12Z, 50.1% at the 12:14Z bucket, then 100% from 12:16Z onward through 13:56Z (mean 58.42). This is the real, hidden failure signal.

payment_success_rate collapsed in the same window: ~99.17% at 12:04Z, partial 38.93% at 12:12Z bucket, then ~2.1-2.7% from 12:20Z onward (min 1.44, last 2.13). Customer transfers essentially stopped succeeding.

payment-service ERROR logs begin at 12:15:27Z and are dominated by two signatures: 'mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (140 occurrences, first 12:15:27Z) and 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' (171 occurrences, first 12:16:44Z). Payments are marked PENDING_RETRY rather than failed.

A cert-watcher warning at 11:50:26Z foreshadowed the expiry: 'client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires in 25 minutes (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z)'. The first transfer failure (12:15:27Z) follows the 12:15:00Z cert expiry by ~27 seconds.

payment-service latency_p99_ms DROPPED rather than rose during the incident: ~320-327ms before 12:04Z, falling to ~132-144ms from 12:20Z onward. Resource metric cpu_pct was flat at ~30% (27.41-34.25) across 11:00-14:00Z, showing no resource saturation — consistent with fast TLS-handshake rejection rather than overload.

bank-partner-api is an external dependency with NO logs/metrics of its own; it can only be observed through its callers (payment-service). This means any 'bank side' claim must be inferred from payment-service's outbound call metrics.

events.description: Could not retrieve payment-service resource trends (db_pool_in_use, request_rate, memory_pct) or callback/queue-depth/retry-count signals for 11:00-14:00Z: the tool budget was exhausted after tc-016, returning 'budget_exhausted' for tc-017/018/019.

No dedicated metric named for outbound connection timeouts, retry counts, queue depth, or async callback failure rate was verified as existing on payment-service. available_metrics returned only: bank_api_error_rate, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, payment_success_rate, request_rate, restarts.
Did not check whether other services (e.g. api-gateway, other callers of bank-partner-api, or neighbouring services) show the same symptom, since budget ran out.

events.answer: Customer-reported transfer failures began at ~12:15:27Z (bank-partner-api certificate expiring at exactly 12:15:00Z), when payment-service's mTLS client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expired, causing 100% of outbound bank-partner-api calls to fail TLS handshake. The "green" payment-service error_rate panel is NOT trustworthy: it measures HTTP 5xx (flat ~0.2%), while transfer failures are recorded as async PENDING_RETRY, not 5xx. The true symptom is visible in bank_api_error_rate (0.2% → 100% at 12:14Z) and payment_success_rate (99% → ~2.5%). Failures affect the payment→bank-partner-api transfer path, not payment-service CPU/mem.

events.title: Expired client certificate for bank-partner-api mTLS (our side)
settlement-service v1.9.0 CSV exporter saturates shared ledger-db / kafka
bank.api.timeout_ms raise (3000->5000) at 11:20Z causes the failures

events.summary: H1 is well grounded end-to-end on verified findings: cert notAfter=12:15:00Z, an independent cert-watcher warning at 11:50:26Z, first failure 27s after expiry, and payment-service logs explicitly containing 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' (F11). Temporal order is tight (12:15:00Z expiry → 12:14–12:16Z onset), and scope matches the single affected path (payment-service→bank-partner-api, the only user of that cert). Alternatives are positively contradicted, not merely dismissed: H2 cannot produce an alert 45 naming our own certificate/CN, and H3/H4 cannot produce TLS-layer rejections 45–105 min after their trigger events. The green dashboard is explained by async PENDING_RETRY vs an HTTP-5xx-only panel (F8). Residual weaknesses are non-blocking: the 'cert was not rotated' claim is inferred from absence in a tool that cannot surface rotations (there is no credential-rotation tool), and blast radius beyond payment-service was left unchecked. Both warrant a confidence cap, not another round. Decisive evidence for H2 would require bank-partner-api telemetry that is permanently absent (has_telemetry=false, tc-015 not_found), so no further query would change the ranking.

events.why: top hypothesis is above threshold and clearly ahead

critiques.summary: H1 is well grounded end-to-end on verified findings: cert notAfter=12:15:00Z, an independent cert-watcher warning at 11:50:26Z, first failure 27s after expiry, and payment-service logs explicitly containing 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' (F11). Temporal order is tight (12:15:00Z expiry → 12:14–12:16Z onset), and scope matches the single affected path (payment-service→bank-partner-api, the only user of that cert). Alternatives are positively contradicted, not merely dismissed: H2 cannot produce an alert 45 naming our own certificate/CN, and H3/H4 cannot produce TLS-layer rejections 45–105 min after their trigger events. The green dashboard is explained by async PENDING_RETRY vs an HTTP-5xx-only panel (F8). Residual weaknesses are non-blocking: the 'cert was not rotated' claim is inferred from absence in a tool that cannot surface rotations (there is no credential-rotation tool), and blast radius beyond payment-service was left unchecked. Both warrant a confidence cap, not another round. Decisive evidence for H2 would require bank-partner-api telemetry that is permanently absent (has_telemetry=false, tc-015 not_found), so no further query would change the ranking.

challenges.issue: The claim 'no rotation occurred' rests on absence of a rotation event in a config-change tool that does not model credential rotation; no credential-rotation/secret-manager source exists. It is an unverified assumption, though the expiry timestamp and alert 45 text are direct observations independent of it.

Blast radius is unverified: it was not checked whether any other caller of bank-partner-api (or api-gateway's transfer route) shows the same failures. This would only tighten the already-strong conclusion and does not affect the origin identified.

H2 names a different origin but is contradicted by direct evidence (alert 45 naming our client cert and CN, plus a 25-min-prior predicted expiry from our own config). Its only decisive discriminator — bank-partner-api's own health — is permanently unobservable (has_telemetry=false), so this is genuine contradiction rather than an untested equal.

Dismissal is justified by contradiction, not by test: no ledger-db/kafka resource or writer-service signal was ever measured, so the 'other writers are healthy' implication is asserted. Still, the chain requires TLS alert 45 output, which datastore contention cannot produce, so it cannot rank first.
